why: flow.py's value is its ruleset, not its plumbing. PROBE_JS, the drive_controls click-and-fingerprint strategy and the planted-defect selftest are the parts worth keeping and would port almost verbatim onto a Playwright page. Only the cdp.WS dependency underneath is the build-vs-buy question, and it belongs to tools/browser. Verdict from the shared analysis: split  -  replace cdp.py's hand-rolled CDP transport (WS class + launch/new_tab machinery, cdp.py:69-363, ~300 of 509 lines) with Playwright's Python sync API; keep cdp.py's chrome_path()/adopt-running-instance CLI subcommands for its separate authenticated-ad-hoc-browsing job (or point them at Playwright's connect_over_cdp() later, out of this scope). Keep flow.py's PROBE_JS ruleset, drive_controls click-and-fingerprint fuzz strategy, and the planted-defect selftest almost verbatim  -  rehost them on a Playwright page/context instead of cdp.WS, add a webkit context alongside chromium, wire tracing.start/stop plus screenshot-on-FAIL, and enable pytest-xdist parallelism.

alternatives.name: Playwright (Python sync API, PyPI package `playwright`, Microsoft, MIT)
alternatives.covers: Auto-waiting/actionability checks replace our fixed time.sleep() waits (flow.py:413,526-530,739,767) as the flakiness source. Real cross-browser: chromium AND webkit browser types (webkit is Apple's WebKit engine on Windows/Linux, not just a spoofed Chrome UA the way flow.py's VIEWPORTS mobile UA string is today, flow.py:95-105)  -  this is the one gap our tool cannot close by itself since it only ever drives Chrome. Built-in device descriptors (playwright.devices['iPhone 13']: 390x844 viewport, dsf 3, isMobile+hasTouch true) match what we hand-specified almost exactly, confirming this was already a solved problem. Trace viewer (context.tracing.start/stop -> trace.zip: DOM snapshot, network, console, source per action, viewable via `playwright show-trace` or trace.playwright.dev) and config-level screenshot='only-on-failure' + video='retain-on-failure' directly fill the 'no artifact on FAIL' gap in flow.py. aria_snapshot()/to_match_aria_snapshot() diffs the real computed accessibility tree, a stronger check than our DOM-heuristic label/name checks. pytest-playwright + pytest-xdist (`pytest --numprocesses auto`) gives real worker parallelism our single-Page architecture cannot. Cross-platform browser install also removes the exact uncertainty ship-gate.yml documents about itself today (.github/workflows/ship-gate.yml:36-46,205-224: browser-instrument-selftest is windows-latest-only and 'has NOT been confirmed' Chrome exists at cdp.py's hardcoded path)  -  a Playwright-backed flow.py could run in the SAME ubuntu-latest job as the rest of the gate. Also directly supports connect_over_cdp() for cdp.py's OTHER job (attaching to an already-running authenticated Chrome), so that use case is not stranded.
alternatives.gap: Does not provide our bespoke test STRATEGY: the WCAG-tuned PROBE_JS ruleset and the 'click every control once per fresh load, judge by state-fingerprint diff' fuzz strategy are our own design with no off-the-shelf Playwright equivalent  -  Playwright gives primitives (locator.click(), page.evaluate()), not this auto-discovery-and-fuzz approach. The JS itself is copy-paste portable into page.evaluate() with zero rewrite. webkit browser type is engine-family parity with Safari, not literally iOS Mobile Safari on a real device (no real device farm without a paid service, out of scope here).
alternatives.cost: New PyPI dependency + one-time `playwright install chromium webkit` download (~281MB + ~180MB per playwright.dev/docs/browsers), breaks the stated stdlib-only house habit (explicitly a habit, not a hard rule here). Cacheable via PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH + actions/cache keyed on the pinned version; confirmed to work fully offline once cached (playwright.dev/docs/browsers). Free/MIT, no paid tier. Notably de-risked in-house already: this exact tool family (@playwright/mcp via bunx, a playwright-cli skill) is already used elsewhere in this operator's own Codex-side tooling for a related job (dot-codex/bin/playwright-mcp-obscura, dot-codex/skills/web-inspect/SKILL.md) and is the sole SOTA tool this operator's own canonical rubric prescribes for E2E/visual/a11y (work-docs/SOTA-TESTING-CRITERIA-2026.md sections 3.D and appendix).

alternatives.name: Puppeteer (Node/JS, Google)
alternatives.covers: Chromium auto-wait, screenshots, basic device emulation.
alternatives.gap: No official Python binding  -  a foreign JS/Node runtime bolted onto a Python-stdlib repo, purely to get less than Playwright already gives natively from Python. Chromium-only (same single-engine gap as ours), no built-in trace viewer, no accessibility-tree assertion API, no first-party parallel test runner.
alternatives.cost: Requires Node/bun toolchain plus a subprocess bridge from Python for strictly less capability than Playwright's direct Python binding  -  not worth the added toolchain given Playwright exists.

alternatives.name: Selenium 4 (Python package `selenium` + Selenium Manager)
alternatives.covers: True cross-browser via W3C WebDriver (Chrome, Firefox, real Safari via safaridriver on macOS, Edge), Python-native, mature and boring in the good sense, free.
alternatives.gap: No auto-waiting by default  -  explicit WebDriverWait/expected_conditions needed almost everywhere, i.e. the same class of fixed-wait flakiness risk our own code already has, just relocated rather than solved. No trace-viewer equivalent. Weaker first-party parallelism (Selenium Grid or pytest-xdist bolted on, no built-in device-descriptor dict as rich as Playwright's). Directional third-party benchmarking found in this research (single unverified secondary source, treat as indicative not exact) put Playwright faster and less flaky than Selenium in 2026 comparisons.
alternatives.cost: Free, Windows-friendly, driver management now automatic via Selenium Manager (smaller download footprint than Playwright's full browser set, but still a network-fetched binary, same offline-caching consideration).

alternatives.name: Cypress
alternatives.covers: Strong developer experience, built-in retry-ability for assertions, screenshot/video on failure.
alternatives.gap: JS/TS runner only, no official Python binding (same foreign-runtime cost as Puppeteer here). WebKit support is comparatively limited next to Playwright's. Mobile 'device emulation' is viewport-resize only, no separate touch/UA device-descriptor richness. Historically weaker multi-tab/cross-origin support than Playwright.
alternatives.cost: Free OSS core (paid Cypress Cloud tier only for dashboards/orchestration, not required locally); still a second Node-based toolchain in a Python-first repo. Named only in this operator's own SOTA rubric's tool-inventory appendix, not in the prescribed E2E/a11y pack (work-docs/SOTA-TESTING-CRITERIA-2026.md section 3.D names Playwright there).

evidence: Read tools/e2e/flow.py (1143 lines) and tools/browser/cdp.py (509 lines) in full, and read the Playwright, Selenium and Puppeteer project docs. `python tools/e2e/flow.py selftest` passes today against a real Chrome install with no third-party package present. Nothing was installed to produce this record, so the migration line counts are estimates from reading, not from a port.
recheck: pip install playwright && playwright install chromium webkit, then port flow.py's Page class (flow.py:459-549) to open a Playwright BrowserContext per viewport (chromium for 'mobile'/'desktop', webkit added) instead of cdp.WS, keep PROBE_JS verbatim inside page.evaluate(), and rerun `python tools/e2e/flow.py selftest`  -  verdict holds if the ported version still catches all 11 planted defects with 0 false positives (matching today's baseline) AND additionally produces a trace.zip/screenshot on every FAIL-level finding AND completes a webkit pass with no new false positives on the clean fixture page.
what_ours_does: cdp.py is a from-scratch WebSocket+CDP client (cdp.py:194-360, hand-rolled RFC6455 framing, masking, fragmentation, ping/pong) plus a Chrome launcher that only knows three hardcoded Windows paths (CHROME_CANDIDATES, cdp.py:55-59) and has logic to adopt an already-running Chrome on the automation profile rather than spawn a second one (cdp.py:122-169)  -  that adoption logic exists for a DIFFERENT job than E2E testing: letting a Claude session browse authenticated pages (cdp.py `text`/`shot`/`eval` subcommands, docstring lines 1-33), which flow.py's audit reuses incidentally. flow.py layers an E2E/accessibility auditor on top: a ~320-line in-page JS probe (PROBE_JS, flow.py:120-439) that checks render/overflow/tap-target-size/name/label/contrast/text-size/image/viewport-meta defects with WCAG-tuned thresholds; a driver (drive_controls, flow.py:725-809) that clicks every visible control once per fresh page load and judges the effect via an 11-field before/after state fingerprint plus network/dialog/exception capture; console/network/exception classification (browser_findings, flow.py:564-639); and a selftest (flow.py:1014-1106) that serves a page with 11 planted defects and asserts each is caught with zero false positives on a clean page. It only ever drives one real installed Chrome, one page at a time, with fixed time.sleep() waits (flow.py:413, 526-530, 739, 767) instead of actionability/network-idle waiting, and never captures a screenshot, video, or trace on a failing flow  -  every FAIL finding today is a bare text string plus a CSS selector.
strongest_counterargument: Today's 1652 lines cost zero dependencies and zero network access  -  `python tools/e2e/flow.py selftest` passes right now with only a real Chrome install already on the machine. Playwright adds a ~460MB one-time download (chromium+webkit), a pinned-version cache-warm step in CI, and a new failure surface (cache-miss forces a live download, which is not actually 'offline' on day one)  -  a real, permanent maintenance cost for a one-person-maintained repo. And the concrete gap this migration closes hardest  -  WebKit-engine coverage  -  has not been shown to have caught a single real defect in this operator's actual deployed apps yet (unknown/unverified); the case for migrating is a credible risk-reduction argument backed by named architectural gaps (fixed sleeps, Chromium-only, no artifact-on-fail, no parallelism, a CI job already flagged as an unconfirmed Windows-only assumption in ship-gate.yml), not a proven-necessary one from an observed missed bug.
_shared_analysis: tools/e2e and tools/browser were reviewed together because flow.py's only third-party-replaceable dependency is cdp.py's transport.
